seoDescription: OpenGov.kz is an independent civic initiative about open government in Kazakhstan: open data, public budgets and civic participation.

hero.title: Open Government in Kazakhstan
hero.questions: How can you find out what the government spends money on? Where can you find open data? How can you propose changes to a draft legal act?
hero.intro: OpenGov.kz is an independent civic initiative. We are developing a website about open government in Kazakhstan and preparing materials to help people understand transparency and civic participation tools.

items.title: Transparency
items.text: The government discloses information about its decisions, spending and performance. People can find, understand and verify this information.

items.title: Accountability
items.text: Public authorities explain their decisions and are answerable for their consequences. Citizens can ask questions and seek reasoned answers.

items.title: Civic participation
items.text: People can propose solutions and take part in discussions. Public authorities consider proposals and explain what was taken into account and why.

tools.title: Open government tools
tools.intro: You can start by exploring three government portals in Kazakhstan.

items.title: Open Data
items.text: Government datasets for research, analysis and building services.

items.title: Open Budgets
items.text: Budget information for understanding and discussing public spending.

items.title: Open Legal Acts
items.text: Draft legal acts available for review and public discussion.

participate.title: Suggest a topic or help make sense of an issue
participate.p1: Interested in public spending, working with data or studying legislation? We want to bring citizens and experts together to discuss practical improvements.
participate.p2: You can suggest a question for analysis, share your experience or discuss working together.

about.title: About the initiative
about.text: We are currently developing the website and preparing accessible materials about open government. An expert community, collaborative research and public-interest services are areas for future development.
